title: Slow Cooker Cabbage, Potato & White Bean Soup
description: Cabbage, potatoes, and white beans simmer into a simple, filling crockpot soup built from inexpensive grocery staples.
substitutions: Use cannellini, great northern, or navy beans.
Use frozen diced potatoes if that makes prep easier.
Add sliced carrots if you have some to use up.

steps.text: Add everything to the slow cooker.
Cook until the potatoes and cabbage are tender.

cookSteps.text: Put 4 cups chopped cabbage, 3 cups diced potatoes, 2 cans drained white beans, 1 can diced tomatoes, 5 cups broth, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning if using into the slow cooker.
Stir, cover, and cook on LOW for about 6 hours or HIGH for 3–4 hours, until the potatoes and cabbage are tender.
Taste and season as needed. For a thicker soup, mash a few potatoes and beans against the side of the cooker before serving.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat with a splash of broth or water if needed.

title: Sheet-Pan Zucchini, Chickpea & Cheddar Melts
description: Roasted zucchini and chickpeas get a cheesy finish for an easy meatless sheet-pan dinner.

ingredients.item: flour tortillas or slices of toast for serving

substitutions: Use yellow summer squash instead of zucchini.
Use white beans instead of chickpeas.
Use Monterey Jack or mozzarella instead of cheddar.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss 2 sliced zucchini and 2 cans drained chickpeas with 1 tablespoon oil and 1 teaspoon garlic powder on a large sheet pan.
Spread into one layer and roast 20 minutes, stirring once halfway through.
Sprinkle 1 cup shredded cheddar over the vegetables and chickpeas. Return to the oven for 3–5 minutes, until melted.
Serve as-is in bowls or spoon onto tortillas or toast if using.

storage: Refrigerate the roasted mixture up to 4 days. Reheat in a skillet, oven, or microwave; add fresh cheese after reheating if desired.

title: Leftover Mac & Cheese Broccoli Skillet
description: Leftover macaroni and cheese becomes a quick skillet meal with broccoli and a crisp cheesy top.
substitutions: Use frozen broccoli; thaw or microwave it briefly first.
Use peas or chopped leftover vegetables instead of broccoli.
Use any melty cheese you already have.

steps.text: Steam the broccoli in the skillet.
Add the leftover mac and heat through.

cookSteps.text: Put 1 1/2 cups small broccoli florets and 2 tablespoons milk or water in a large skillet. Cover and cook over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until bright green and nearly tender.
Add 2 cups leftover macaroni and cheese and black pepper if using. Stir gently and cook 4–5 minutes, until everything is hot.
Sprinkle with up to 1/2 cup shredded cheddar if using, cover for about 1 minute to melt, then serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days after making, provided the original macaroni and cheese was still within its safe refrigerated storage window. Reheat until steaming hot.

title: Small-Batch Banana Peanut Butter Oat Cups
description: A ripe banana, peanut butter, and oats make six soft baked oat cups for breakfast or an easy snack.
substitutions: Use quick oats instead of old-fashioned oats.
Use sunflower seed butter if peanut butter is not suitable.
Add a small handful of raisins or chocolate chips if desired.

steps.text: Mix the banana, peanut butter, and wet ingredients.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease 6 muffin cups. Mash 1 large ripe banana in a bowl, then stir in 1/4 cup peanut butter, 1 egg, 1/2 cup milk, and 2 tablespoons brown sugar or maple syrup if using.
Stir in 1 1/4 cups oats and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon if using. Let the mixture stand 2 minutes so the oats begin absorbing the liquid.
Divide among 6 muffin cups and bake 18–20 minutes, until set in the centers.
Cool 5 minutes before lifting the oat cups from the pan.

storage: Refrigerate up to 5 days or freeze up to 2 months. Reheat briefly or eat chilled.
